overview: The Homestay Scheme for Rural Tourism is a sub-scheme under Swadesh Darshan 2.0, aimed at developing homestays in tribal areas to promote responsible tourism and enhance livelihood opportunities for tribal communities. It provides funding support for the development and renovation of tribal homestays and village community requirements, creating community-based responsible tourism through cultural exchange between tourists and indigenous people. The scheme is implemented under the Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan (PMJUGA) and targets the development of 1000 homestays in tribal areas.
objectives: Develop homestays in tribal areas to promote responsible tourism
Enhance livelihood opportunities for tribal communities
Create community-based responsible tourism through cultural exchange
Provide authentic tribal rural experience for tourists
Encourage states/UTs to provide further assistance to uplift local livelihood
Develop tourism potential in tribal villages
Promote entrepreneurship and self-employment in tourism value chain
Ensure convergence with existing Government of India/State/UT schemes
eligibility: The State Government / UT Administrations shall be required to identify suitable tribal village(s) and tribal beneficiary(ies) in the tribal areas for construction/renovation of homestays. This shall be done in consultation with the local community. State Government / UT Administration shall give priority to establish Home stays in the Dharti Aaba villages. However the same can be established in nearby suitable tribal villages after exhausting this possibility, with the intention that the Dharti Aaba villages will also be benefitted under ripple effect. Further, under the secondary impact, tribals from Dharti Aaba villages can also be trained and involved to provide services including hospitality, guides, cultural shows etc. Selection of villages should be done with the objective to provide awareness for Livelihood while preserving and celebrating culture of tribal communities. Similarly, the State Governments/UTAs shall identify required interventions for the village community where homestays are proposed for funding to enhance tourism potential of the identified village and the same may be included in the project proposal.
benefits: Funding support for development & renovation of Tribal Homestays and village community requirements. Creation of community-based responsible tourism in tribal villages through cultural exchange between tourists and indigenous people. Authentic tribal rural experience for tourists. Encouragement for states/UTs to provide further assistance required to uplift the livelihood of the local community. Opportunity for tribal households to generate alternate livelihood through homestay operations. Capacity building and training for tribal beneficiaries in hospitality, guiding, and cultural shows. Integration of feedback mechanism on promotional websites/platforms. Periodic data collection on revenue generation, occupancy, and feedback received.
financial_support: The Government of India will provide 100% of the funds for the identified components of the project. The central funding under the scheme shall be routed through the Implementing Agency designated by the State/UT. The Implementing Agency will also be responsible to disburse funds to individual beneficiaries / village communities in a well-defined and transparent manner. The funds would be released to the Implementing Agency of the concerned States/UTs after in-principle approval of the projects by the Ministry of Tourism. States/UTs will submit one project to the Ministry of Tourism under this scheme which may include proposal for cluster(s) of villages comprising of five-six (5-6) villages in a cluster and 5-10 homestays in each village. A maximum of Rs. 5 crores may be provided to each State/UT. For exceptional projects, the Ministry of Tourism (MoT) may propose a higher allocation upto Rs. 2 crore to the best performing States/UTs. The decision of MoT on the amount to be approved for the project shall be final. Higher allocation would be considered only in those cases where States have been able to exhaust the upper ceiling (of Rs. 5.00 Crore) and post recommendation of Mission Directorate and Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee. The funding under the scheme cannot be utilized for land acquisition, resettlement and rehabilitation, relocation, dredging/development of bunds of a water body (man-made & natural both) etc.
application_process: 1. States/UTs shall identify suitable tribal villages with tourism potential and tribal beneficiaries for homestay development in consultation with local community. 2. States/UTs shall prioritize Dharti Aaba villages for homestay establishment. 3. States/UTs shall identify required interventions for village community to enhance tourism potential. 4. States/UTs shall prepare project proposal as per the Model Template (Annexure-I) including preference to female homestay owners, model homestay design according to local vernacular architecture, marketing plan, convergence with central and state schemes, development of community space, and capacity building plan. 5. States/UTs shall submit the project proposal on the portal (sd2.tourism.gov.in) with covering letter of State/UT Tourism Secretary as per timeline communicated by Ministry of Tourism. 6. In case of any issues related to proposal submission on the portal, States/UTs may submit the proposal on email id swadesh.darshan@gov.in and inform the same to the Ministry. 7. Proposals meeting guidelines shall be placed before Mission Directorate (MD) for review and recommendation to Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC). 8. CSMC after due examination will grant approval to the project and further, the project will be sanctioned by the Ministry of Tourism. 9. State Government has to implement the project as per approved project proposal and scheme guidelines. 10. In case of any revisions in the project, approval of CSMC will be obtained.
required_documents: Covering letter of State/UT Tourism Secretary
Model homestay design / prototype according to local vernacular architecture
Marketing Plan for identified tribal villages or cluster
Convergence with central and state schemes
Development of community space in each identified tribal village
Capacity Building Plan for homestay owners
deadlines: As per timeline communicated by the Ministry of Tourism from time to time
implementing_agency: State Government / UT Administrations (to designate Implementing Agency)
caveats: Funding under the scheme cannot be utilized for land acquisition, resettlement and rehabilitation, relocation, dredging/development of bunds of a water body (man-made & natural both)
States/UTs must ensure convergence of various central and state schemes while identification of villages and homestays
State/UT shall ensure that the proposed land parcel for development of homestays is in possession of beneficiary with clear ownership title and available for development
State/UT shall ensure that the identified homestay owner belongs to the tribal community

The State/UT shall be responsible for providing requisite capacity building support (upskilling/reskilling) to beneficiaries during development phase and further responsible for marketing and promotion of developed homestays under the scheme

The State/UT shall also partner with experienced NGO/Rural Tourism Societies etc to support in identification of tribal villages, tribal households, undertake stakeholder consultations, sensitization of homestay owners, community development, and overall project implementation through its own resources

The State/UTs may also assist for upgrading the hospitality experience from state/UT funds where ever required and further encourage stakeholders to adopt sustainable tourism practices in tribal villages
Technical upskilling and training of homestay owners should be done by States/UTs in collaboration with IHMs, SIHMs and Ministry of Tribal Affairs etc

Once homestays and community spaces are operational, State Governments/UTs will feature them on their promotional websites/platforms along with photographs and testimonials and make necessary efforts to integrate feedback mechanism
State Government will periodically collect data regarding regular operation of homestays developed under the scheme including revenue generation, occupancy, feedback received etc
